23 Pack Resistance Bands Set Workout Bands, 5 Stackable Exercise Bands 5 Loop Resistance Bands 2 Core Sliders – Door Anchor Handles Ankle Straps Carry Bag Instant Cooling Towel Wrist Wraps I normally don't review products this soon. I just recieved the items today.

Ankle straps. Wow! They're comfortable. I really want expecting much for this price range, and the ankle straps are definitely worth it. Time will tell how durable they are, but I think I'll get my money's worth out of them.

Wrist wraps. Again, I wasn't expecting much. Never used wrist straps before, but I did choose this bundle because, hey what the heck, they're included. I don't have experience using the wrist straps, so I have no idea how they compare to others. They do provide support to my wrists. The thumb loop should have been sewn in so that it wraps nicely around your thumb though. Instead there's the one side that had to fold over because it was sewn as a flat loop. I'll give them a try.

Resistance loops. They're thin. I guess I was expecting them to be a little thicker. They do give resistance and I'm sure I'll find ways to use them. The heavier ones do make me sore on the outsides of my thighs, so they are doing what they're intended for, adding resistance.

Resistance bands. They're thin. They do seem to have the appropriate ratings though compared to other more expensive resistance bands that I have. I was looking for bands with these kind of attachment points. They're more versatile than the ones that have to hook into their own proprietary handles and attachments.

I do wish that they sold sets of just the bands though. Because there's not enough of the higher weight bands in this set for all of my needs. I'll end up buying other set just for extra bands.

The towel. A decent towel for working out. Again, I've never used one in the gym. But I'll find a use for it.

Door anchor. This thing is not going to slip through the door unintentionally. Just remember to put it through the hinge side of the door. Doors don't have enough strength on the latch side or top.

Sliders. They're about the same size and basic construction as another set of sliders that I have. But the ones in this set seem to be tacky on the smooth side. So if you're using them on carpet, you'll need to wear shoes or socks with some grip. Otherwise, you're foot will slide off and the slider will stay put.

And just one general complaint. There are several pictures of overly photoshopped Asian models demonstrating the different items on the packaging and instructions. They're photoshopped to look caucasian. I don't care if your Asian, African, European, South American, American or what have you. I buy a product for being in an acceptable price to quality ratio that works for me. If I like it, I buy again. I don't care who is making it or selling it.
text_fidelity_b: 23 Pack Resistance Bands Set Workout Bands, 5 Stackable Exercise Bands 5 Loop Resistance Bands 2 Core Sliders – Door Anchor Handles Ankle Straps Carry Bag Instant Cooling Towel Wrist Wraps

text_fidelity_a:
Lightspeed Outdoors 2 Person PVC-Free Air Bed Mattress for Camping and Travel I have a SoundAsleep air mattress that is wonderful in terms of comfort and durability. However, it's way too cumbersome to take anywhere - heavy, bulky and not at all portable. This air mattress, while it lacks some of the niceties of the SoundAsleep, is a breeze to carry along.

The build quality is very good. The casing is sturdy and, while a ground sheet is never a bad idea for protection (and insulation), the material is thick enough to deal with rocks without a puncture.

It includes a battery powered air pump that runs off of 4D cells. It's not bad and it gets the job done, but I would have liked to have an AC option in addition to battery power (or perhaps a Li-ion battery option for more power). Still, even with the 4D cells, I was able to fully inflate the mattress in a little over 2 minutes (2 min, 32 seconds, to be exact). I found that to be satisfactory performance. The pump can also be used to deflate the mattress.

The inflation port can be completely removed for quick deflation. You can also open just the top portion of the port, which is a one-way valve (you can add air, but it won't come out). The port is well-made, sturdy and easy to use.

Comfort is pretty good. This is a thin mattress, so don't expect an ultra cushy experience. I found it to be the most comfortable when it was slightly less than fully inflated. Adding the foam topper (which is sold separately:[[ASIN:B00U2VI1A8 Lightspeed Outdoors Foam Topper for Air Mattresses, Maroon]]) makes for a better experience. But even as-is, I would rate this as pretty comfortable (and miles better than not having it at all!).

It rolls up easily and stows in a carry bag. The bag is big enough so you don't have to be super careful in how the mattress is folded/rolled to get it to fit inside. The carry bag is sturdy, and large enough to also hold the inflation pump.

If you're looking for a very easy to tote mattress that provides for a decent amount of comfort, this is well worth considering.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Lightspeed Outdoors 2 Person PVC-Free Air Bed Mattress for Camping and Travel

text_fidelity_a:
Sunny Health & Fitness Twisting Stair Stepper Machine with Handlebar and Digital Display This just arrived so it's too soon to say, but I REALLY miss my Aspen stepper that lasted forever and would probably still be going strong if I hadn't lent it to my kids who left it out in the rain and ruined it.

PROS: It was relatively easy to assemble; it's made of steel rather than plastic; it has a built in timer (also a scan, calorie counter and stroke counter), but the accuracy of these things is dubious at best, and I'm not one to use them anyway; it doesn't take up much space and is easy to move.

CONS: The tension adjustment knob is a joke. From the easiest to the most difficult setting is so subtle, I barely noticed it. Even at the most difficult setting, going as fast as I could, I didn't perspire at all; for people who are used to steppers, the twisting motion is a bit awkward, and since it came with no exercise instructions, perhaps there's something I'm missing to the advantages of twisting; at full extension, the handle bars don't go up very high, and they don't move.

If you're someone just embarking on an exercise routine, don't want to spend a lot of money and don't have a lot of space, this will probably work just fine. However, for the athletically inclined who already work out regularly, this will probably be a bit of a disappointment.

Update: Have now had this for a while and need to mention that 1) the tension adjustment knob does work but ONLY WORKS IF YOU LET THE STEPPER SIT FOR AT LEAST A COUPLE OF HOURS. If you try adjusting it without letting is sit undisturbed, you will NOT feel any difference; and 2) the 250# weight limit is a joke. My husband, who weighs 195, can't use it at all. If he does, the cable screws (as others have commented) break off. He's handy, so he's been able to fix it each time, but after 3 or 4 times, he just will no longer use it. For me, it's not much of a work out, but I do use it.

Update a little over a year later: The cable broke, and the manufacturer has been unresponsive. So into the trash it sadly goes. Due to a major design flaw in construction, the cable is forced to stretch, wear down and eventually break with use over time. A hydraulic resistance system would be a major design improvement. So if you don't mind a machine that will only last about a year, this stepper is fine. But if you want something that will last longer, I'd give it a miss.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Twisting Stair Stepper Machine with Handlebar and Digital Display

Monstrum 1-4x20 Rifle Scope with Rangefinder Reticle and Medium Profile Scope Rings My second Monstrum, and I don't regret this one. Granted, you can get PrimaryArms for same price (when on sale) but my big thing is, 1" tube diameter. Go ahead and look see how many LPVO's you can find with 1" tube... The glass is OK clear, nothing came loose after shaking it like a maniac for 5 minutes, but didn't do a drop test... yet. The diopter adjustment is ok, even thgouh you might have a tough time if you're in the + side with your vision. Has a mini throw aluminum lever which I loctite'd (new word) - makes the zoom wheel turning fairly easy. On the left side, this proof that proof message in white letters is clearly visible when you mount the scope, so that's a little cheap looking, maybe I'll cover it with a sticker. Also, comes with this weird battery (two of them) - not your standard 2032 or 2025. Has orange "glass" bikini lense cover, which is a'right - keeps things from getting overly dusty. The reticle, not my super fav, but illuminates abundantly in both red and green - 5 settings each with no 0 stops between levels with the knob set on the left at 45 degree angle, close to the eye viewer. Turning was ok - not too hard, however the battery door gasket will bunch up on you if you tighten it fast and furious, so three finger it, Mercedes logo style, slowly. Windage and elevation turrets are small to medium height, and very nicely clikety and tactile, even though they don't snap on a setting like a swiss clock - so it's a bit mushy. And scope rings are included - medium size.

Bottom line, a head turner it is not. But, it doesn't need to be. Hopefully, gets the job done, after going on a 44mag lever with full loads, not Special. That'll really bang it around good, hoping it'll come out alright and keep on ticking.
text_fidelity_b: Monstrum 1-4x20 Rifle Scope with Rangefinder Reticle and Medium Profile Scope Rings

LeupoldRX-1200i Rangefinder Matte This range finder is excellent. Leupold has packed a lot of features into a range finder for under $200. I ranged on some known distances and it was right on as far as accuracy goes. I did not test it past 500 meters but im sure you could really push this one out and still have good accuracy. I like the automatic True Ballistic Range calculation--it really lends itself well to hunting with rifle or bow. I also use this range finder's LOS settings for photography-related hobbies. Knowing distances of natural objects in a scene can help with prime lens choice, etc. This range finder is useful everywhere. In addition to being an awesome range finder, it makes for a great monocular. I find myself using it a lot while hunting rather than pulling up big, heavy binoculars. The magnification and clarity of the optic is great--which is to be expected from leupold.

I really like the case that came with the range finder. It carries the unit very well and it also has a card spot for carrying a range card. It actually includes a range card and a micro fiber cloth for cleaning your optics. Last but not least, the unit came with a battery. It is nice being able to take this out of the box and immediately use it. I bought [[ASIN:B0057ILX8S these batteries]] to use in it after the original is dead. The original that came with the unit is an energizer brand.

Dimensions of the case and the range finder unit can be seen in the photos I have uploaded

Included:
-Range finder unit
-Micro Fiber cloth
-Range Reference Card
-Carrying case (unit pocket, range card slot)
-Manual

Pros:
*Extremely accurate ranging
*TBR calculations
*Bow, Rifle, and LOS options
*Small and light
*Waterproof

Cons:
*None

Additional Considerations:
Leupold makes very solid optic-related products. You cannot really go wrong with them. They do well by their customers from what I have experienced and observed.

Overall: 5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 5 stars

text_fidelity_a: Rough Rider Folder Denim Micarta RR2181 I have a soft spot for traditional folding knives.  And Wharncliffes.. This is both.  It's also a good quality, super sharp, stainless slipjoint folder with a half stop and a Micarta handle.  For 20 bucks (or at least that's around what I paid for it).  This knife is at  a sweet spot in terms of size.  Any larger and it would start to need a clip and sort of cease to be "pocket friendly".  I mean what else can I say.. I was skeptical of the Rough Rider brand but they really are well made for the money.  I also bought a peanut for my wife and it, too is built to a high standard.  For some folks, half stops are a must.  I generally find them irritating and that may be my only gripe with this blade.  The nail nicks are too sharp to put half stops in this blade.  The blade starts to shift into the half stop and the nick twists and sometimes breaks the edge of my thumbnail.  I thought I was imagining this so i tried it with my pointer finger and sure enough, after pulling the blade a few times, the edge of my fingernail would break.  I may file or polish the edge of the nick a bit and that would solve the issue.  The blade sticks out enough that I can just grab it most of the time without the nail nick.  A slight thumb cutout on one scale would improve this .  Oh, and I could do without it being stainless.  I greatly prefer sharpening carbon steel, but that's just personal preference. Overall this knife will be a great work knife and would delight any wood worker.
text_fidelity_b: Rough Rider Folder Denim Micarta RR2181

RUB1ZR0 Red Green Dot Reflex Sight Scope Adjustable Reticle with 20mm Rail Mount This scope came in an excellent package with tools and batteries (1 installed and 1 extra) and instructions on how to set it up. There are 3 brightness settings for both red and green lasers and choice of red or green lasers on top of the scope and in back of the lens. The G and R letters are the Off positions. Keeping the Off position set when not using it will save battery life. On the top back of the scope are 4 reticle settings by sliding the switch back and forth to choose the one you want to use. All the settings are a little firm to move but stay in place afterwards.

First thing I did was mount the scope and secure to a picatinny rail. After mounting, I used the adjustment screw on top of the scope for elevating the up or down setting. I also used the adjustment screw setting on the left side of scope to zero in the laser. You can do this for up to 100 yards away but make sure you’re on a flat secure surface. I only needed to do small adjustments. This Rub1zro is in my opinion a quality item and a good value for the price.

My garage space is limited and I do not use the bike much, so I prefer the vertical configuration. If you use your bike frequently, it is easier to use the vertical configuration as getting it into the vertical position involves grabbing a dirty tire. The way this keeps the top wheel straight is better than another bike stand that uses a Velcro strap. The bike seems stable, but if I try to push it over I will be able to. I would not consider this kid-friendly in the vertical position.

This distributes the wheel weight well against three round points. Another bike stand I reviewed had the wheel rest against a thin metal bar that looked damaging to the tire.

You have to figure out how to assemble this yourself as there are no assembly instructions, just a parts diagram. They should have included instructions for the wheel rollers. The bottom wheel contact points can be adjusted into six available locations based on the wheel size. Find the correct size before tightening the screws. I did have to adjust the default center location. Adjusting these involves using two Allen wrenches. An improvement would be if there was a place to store the Allen wrenches attached to the product rather than have them mixed in a drawer of assorted Allen wrenches. I will tape the wrenches to the bottom.

The product box was damaged causing a bolt to fall out somewhere along the way. Their customer support team promptly mailed me the missing bolt.

Some of the other reviews on this product page are for a different bike stand. It looks like they swapped products after gathering reviews for the other bike stand. The current price is $70

text_fidelity_a:
Yukon Charlies Carbon Lite Trekking Poles It is important to know that there are poles out there that fold up smaller. But I think these get small enough that they can be held comfortably on your backpack if you have the fancy kind that hold poles. If you want them to fit in your pack, you may need another style, although be warned that the other type I know about fold up in multiple pieces and are bulkier in their own way.

These are three-piece telescoping. The top two sections are held in place with a tensioning lever, much like most bike seats and wheels are held in place. The bottom two sections are held by turning the bottom section so that it pushes up and out a plastic (yes, plastic) interior piece to create friction. Surprisingly, once very tight, you then turn the same section back and forth slightly to turn on or off the "shock absorber".

While I might be skeptical if I only heard about how this works (with the plastic component, and the fact that the shock absorber "switch" is within the same motion as the tightening mechanism), when I examine this item closely, I just can't see anything but great quality. I also cannot break the hold the tightening mechanisms have unless I put unnatural weight on the poles (i.e., more than a normal lean). Also, the two types of cups they give you for the bottom of the poles screw on, which is also nice. Seems like everything is very well thought out and also well executed. And they are super light (so plastic inside is very justified as long as it continues to work, and I guess it will).

Maybe not the preferred style for everyone due to the folded up length, but this style definitely has its advantages. Give these a serious look if you are in the market for this style.
text_fidelity_b: Yukon Charlies Carbon Lite Trekking Poles

text_fidelity_a:
Gaiam Sol Sticky-Grip Yoga Mat (5mm) This yoga mat has a lovely color and attractive patterns embossed in its textured surface. It is well made of high-quality, sustainable, latex-free rubber, and the ribbed bottom works well for preventing slippage on a smooth surface.

This mat out-gassed a slight chemical smell for a few days but it did eventually wear off.

The manufacturer claims this mat is "thick." It seems to me to be about the same thickness, or at best a tiny bit thicker, than the standard rubber mats provided at my gym. For what it is worth, I have this to say about all such mats: If your body doesn't come with it's own built-in "padding," it is a bruising experience to do yoga or calisthenic exercises on a hard floor while sitting or lying on this or any other thin, rubber mat. For that reason, there aren't any yoga mats of this type on the market, including this one, that seem "thick" to me personally. However, since that is a typical design feature among all rubber yoga mats, I am not grading down this mat for not being what I truly consider thick--a depth of three inches. That is the thickness of a different type of yoga mat, a [[ASIN:B003VQNM2I futon mat]], which I also own. The advantage of this mat over a futon mat is that it weighs 5 pounds vs 19 pounds for the futon mat, making it much more portable. It is also substantially easier to keep clean.

Speaking of cleaning this mat, it is not necessary to pay a lot of money for special yoga-mat cleaning solutions when a mat is made of rubber, as this one is. You can make your own quite inexpensively. Here are some examples:

1. Dilute white vinegar in a ratio of 1:16 (1 tablespoon per cup). Vinegar is a natural disinfectant. To increase disinfectant properties, you can add a tablespoon of fresh lemon juice or a few drops of any of the following essential oils which each have disinfectant properties: tea tree, eucalyptus, peppermint, lavender, oregano, lemon, and clove.

2. Dilute a biodegradeable liquid soap, such as [[ASIN:B00016QTYO Sal Suds]], in the same proportion as the white vinegar, 1:16.

3. You can add 1 tablespoon liquid soap to each cup of white-vinegar mixture to maximize cleaning effectiveness.

Instructions for use of cleaning solutions:

1. Put the cleaning solution of your choice in a spray bottle and shake well.

2. Spray the mat and use a clean rag or paper towel to scrub the mat.

3. If you use a soap mixture, you may want to go back over the mat with a clean, damp rag or damp paper towel in order to remove the soap residue. This is not necessary when you use a vinegar mixture.

Note that rubber is not harmed by water. This means that, if you wanted to, you could hose it off on your patio during warm-weather seasons and drape it over a patio chair or the rail of a deck or porch to dry.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Sol Sticky-Grip Yoga Mat (5mm)

text_fidelity_a:
Rixen & Kaul KlickFix Light Clip I have a big beach cruiser bike that I use for most of my transportation needs. I live on my boat in southern California so biking works very well for me.

I had an issue with my bike headlight casting shadows of my bike basket when riding at night and, if I have stuff in the basket, the light can be blocked. I bought this device to move the light to the front edge of the basket so the light would not shine through the basket.

Unfortunately it does not fit well on my standard Wald bike basked. I am sure it fits fine on the type of basked shown in the photo on the Amazon page but that type of basket provides a much flatter surface for this device to grab onto. With the Wald type basket the top rim is a thick wire and the smaller wires that make up the basked itself are bent around the wire rim. This device ends up attaching so poorly that it can move around when riding the bike. Having the headlight spontaneously aiming in different directions is not helpful.

I have managed to make it work by adding some plastic material under the clamp of this device but its not a cosmetically attractive solution and is not as strong as I would like.

This device is very nicely made. They put a lot of attention into the plastic molding but it was obviously not designed for they types of baskets I have always had on my bikes. Ill probably shop around for a new basket but am not sure I can find the type shown in the pictures provided on the amazon page.

It was shipped from Japan so it took a few days to get to me. The seller provided shipping info and the delivery time was OK but not what I usually expect from Amazon Prime.
text_fidelity_b: Rixen & Kaul KlickFix Light Clip

text_fidelity_a:
Westt Mountain Bike Helmet - Bicycle Helmets for Adults with LED Rear Light - Scooter MTB Skateboard Baseball Cycling Helmet Between her roller blades and our eScooters, my wife and I needed two new bike helmets. This was the one we got her and so far, we really like it. I normally do not talk about price points, but in this case: for the price point it feels, looks, and acts like a solid choice. We hope to never have to find out about the "protective" elements, but hope it holds up to that standard as well.

1. The Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light is a good looking helmet, so if looks are important, this has a nice look to it. We like the blue we picked and the overall look is cool.

2. The fit is good. My wife has a smaller head than mine, so we got one that was very adjustable - not really by choice in that we would have order one "size specific" if needed, but again, for her needs. In this case, the Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light allows you to adjust the size in a "one size fits all" situation. The dial on the back adjusts for you and so far it works well. She likes the fit she gets and feels comfortable between that adjustment and the strap.

3. There is no way to "test" this helmet without falling - and we are not test dummies - so we must trust this will have the good if ever needed. She took a good spill once off a SEGWAY and had a helmet on - which truly saved her - and so we swear by wearing head gear. Here I jump to the idea of "You get what you pay for." The helmet we were able to get for me was a far higher price (here on Amazon, over $200), and you CAN tell a difference. BUT, that said, compared to our previous, similarly priced helmets, this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light does seem to have what we need. Would we upgrade? Sure, who wouldn't? BUT, if price is a concern, and for most of us it is, would this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light do the trick? WE THINK SO. Again, there is NO way to know until you need it. BUT this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light fits like the ones we have had in the past and has a similar feel, so we are "trusting" it to take care of her if ever needed.

4. The inside lining IS thinner than mine. There is a difference in that kind of thing - bringing us back to, if we had the money we WOULD upgrade. But for what it is, this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light feels good on her head and she is comfortable.

5. The lights on the back are a huge bonus and work really well. There are (I think) 3 settings for different flashing options and we love that she can do this to bring attention to herself. That said, we have no intention of being out at night, but even in the daylight, it IS something that catches your eye.

In the end and overall we are very pleased with this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light and are happy to have it. Does price matter? You tell me. Yes, there IS a difference for a MUCH higher price point. But if the idea is to get something good on your head to keep you. safe, we think this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light offers us a great option.
text_fidelity_b: Westt Mountain Bike Helmet - Bicycle Helmets for Adults with LED Rear Light - Scooter MTB Skateboard Baseball Cycling Helmet

What I liked:
Compass/divider sets easily and holds firmly. No screw mechanism -- simply pull/push to adjust.

Very sharp points on divider - perfect for measurement work.
Ruling pen and optional holder: I like line work in my field journal, and this makes gorgeous lines with watercolor or ink. Purchased separately, a ruling pen is about $8 USD.
Easily swappable pencil/pen/divider point attachment. I use a compass to frame work in my field journal that is done at magnification.
Additional lead in tube -- nice touch!

What I didn't like...
Absolutely no instructions whatsoever, BUT the tools are intuitive for anyone who has ever used engineering/math compass sets.

Compact Camp Stool Folding Ultralight Portable Mini Chair for Camping Fishing Hiking Gardening Beach Outdoor Chair for Kid Alduts I received this portable camping chair from the manufacturer at no cost for evaluation, and here are my thoughts.

This portable chair is great for camping, backpacking, and attending outdoor events. Weighing les than 2 pounds, it comes in a sturdy storage back with a handle and loops so it can be carried by hand, tucked away with gear, or lashed to a pack without taking much space or adding much weight, and it's so easy to set up my ten year old can do it in about 2 minutes.

The support frame is made of lightweight aircraft aluminum sections attached to each other by shock cord, so you just slip the sections together, secure the ends into the plastic housing, and then attach the ends to the slots in the chair. It's easier if you attach the bottom before the back. When assembled the bottom of the seat is approximately 14" from the ground, the seat is about 21" across, and the back is about 26" high.

I found that the chair sits well on the ground and it feels very stable. The material conforms to the shape of the body so it provides good support, but it does sit very low to the ground so people with arthritis, sciatica, hip problems, or mobility issues might find it difficult to get into or out of without assistance. The chair will support an adult weighting up to 260 pounds, but my 10 year old already decided that it's perfect for her so it's now going to be her chair.

The chair is easy to dissemble and put back in the carry bag, when you're finished using it, and it hardly takes any space at all to store. We really like this chair and think it's perfect for camping, fishing, outdoor concerts or any other outdoor event.

Jueachy Tactical Sling Bag Military Shoulder Molle Chest Pack Shoulder Sling Backpack with USA Flag Patch This is a great sling satchel style bag. It has MOLLE/PALS grids or webbing, whichever your prefer to call it, so you can attach plenty of other equipment to the outside or attach it to another bag itself. MOLLE makes it extremely versatile. It is very well crafted and very durable. The velcro on it isn't cheap and will not wear out quickly like a lot will. I would still recommend using a velcro tool to remove anything you attach to it that way to extend the life of the hook and loop system. One doesn't come with it so if you don't have one anything flat hard plastic will do. High quality zippers were a big plus because when zipping and unzipping the bag it is easy to get the lip of material around the zipper caught and that can damage a cheap zipper.

There are plenty of separate spacious pockets to help keep things divided and organized how you like them. It's just about the perfect size for an additional bag for longer trips or great for an overnight trip somewhere. (I pack light though). Right now it's being used as quick carry bag with my CBRN mask and extra 2 filters and it holds them perfectly. It will not fit a full sized water pouch in it but that's not what these style bags are really designed for.

They should include some kind of instruction for the MOLLE and where to attach the sling to in case people haven't used one like it before. It would've been confusing had I not been familiar with the system and sling bags. Other then that it's a great bag to own.
text_fidelity_b: Jueachy Tactical Sling Bag Military Shoulder Molle Chest Pack Shoulder Sling Backpack with USA Flag Patch

So we took the filter out camping and it preformed really well and the flow rate was superb as well. It took no time at all to filter water for drinking and cooking. Very pleased with my purchase.

Original:

Just received mine today. I set it up in my kitchen suspended from one of the plant hooks of the wife's. Very easy to setup. I did experience a less than ideal flow rate at first. But exactly as the videos from LifeStraw state, the flow rate increases over time. I wasn't really worried about achieving a higher flow rate at this point. It packs to a very similar size. I know my kids and how much water they consume. Ill go through 5 Liters rather quickly. Ill likely also purchase a dirty bladder so that more unfiltered water can be brought to camp at one time. When you have to hike to the supply after a long day hiking, the last thing you want to do is run out.

There are substantial price differences. This swivel version retails for about $60 while the high back is roughly half the price at $34. They both have the same level of comfort (which is passable) and take the same amount of time to assemble (a few minutes to set up and break down). I ultimately would recommend the cheaper version as, clearly, it is half the price and offers the exact same things, unless being able to turn around in circles is a priority for you.

I do enjoy the fact that this can be broken down and stored in a bag. Although it takes more time to put together than your typical camping chair, it’s worth it for it to be compact. Getting the corners of the chair into the poles isn’t incredibly difficult, but it does take some elbow grease; I assume this will become easier with time. I do think having the drink pocket on the front of the chair is a design flaw and the sides of the chair actually come up a bit high to be comfortable for your arms. It swivels incredibly well but again, is that a priority for most people? I don’t really think so. Also, as other reviewers have mentioned, it is a bit wobbly.

Overall, nice idea, but other versions of the chair are better. I particularly like the high back version because it has a pillow which supports your neck and the sides of the chair do not come up as high which is more comfortable.

Fizik Performance Bicycle Bar Tape - Soft, Tacky & Classic Professional Bike Handlebar Tape (2mm, 2.7mm, 3mm) This is a review of the updated Fizik Tempo Microtex Classic (2mm) bar tape. I have been using the old Fizik performance 3mm tacky bar tape on both my road and CX/gravel bikes for several years now, and while that tape was pretty difficult to install (especially on irregular bar shapes) I really liked the look and feel of it and the durability.

This 2mm Microtex tape was much easier to wrap my aero bars with compared to the thick and tacky version I have been using.. but I do prefer the feel of the thicker tacky tape. I can't really speak to the durability of this tape since I've only had it for a few rides but it seems durable when installing it and appears to be easy to clean.

Unfortunately it seems Fizik no longer makes perforated 3mm tacky tape, the new iterations are either flat unperforated tape or grooved channels. I'm not a big fan of the grooved look of the Vento tapes but I may consider using the flat Terra version when I need to rewrap my CX bike.. I really wish they would release a tacky version of the Tempo perforated tape though as I much prefer that look.
text_fidelity_b: Fizik Performance Bicycle Bar Tape - Soft, Tacky & Classic Professional Bike Handlebar Tape (2mm, 2.7mm, 3mm)

Wald Steel Handlebar #803 5.25" 27" 1" Black These are a good product for the price. I purchased them to give myself a little more upright position on an old mountain bike. They do this pretty well.

The reason they do not get 5 stars is the top portion where you put your hand was about 3/4 of an inch too short to mount my original twist shifters and still have room for my grips, making the place where you put your hands a little shorter than intended. OK for me, and also wouldn't be an issue for maybe a different type shifter - like the trigger type, or no shifter at all like a single speed bike. However for someone with very large hands it might be a problem.

Beyond that they appear to be pretty decent quality for the price.

Don't underestimate the amount of change in position that you will get. I paired these with a adjustable quill stem, and I think one or the other would be sufficient, so if your changing out an old mountain bike I might start with one or the other, not both. Also, due to the longer reach you will very likely need to change your shifter and brake cables. My originals were cut too short for this handlebar. Its not a difficult job, but a fair bit of work. You probably will want to buy new grips also in case your originals like mine were hard to remove.
text_fidelity_b: Wald Steel Handlebar #803 5.25" 27" 1" Black

MBB Ab Equipment,Home Ab Machine Function Movement Multiple Core Strength, Abdominal Training 10 in 1 Magic Body Builder with 3 Levels Resistance for Teenage,Women and Men.122 Country Patented I was excited to try this as I love fitness gadgets, and when they added a $10 off coupon, I ordered it even though I read reviews on another brand of the same item from shorter people that it was too big. Turns out for me, they were right. I'm 5' 3", and this is uncomfortable to use to do ab crunches with as it's so long it presses into the top front of my shoulders instead of my upper chest or below, which gets pretty painful after a few reps.

The manufacturer's claim their low resistance level is about 35 pounds of resistance (16kg in pounds) is not true of my unit. I measured the resistance. Moving the smaller side toward the larger only a few inches using a calibrated spring scale, the resistance was 55 pounds - I couldn't move it further as my wrists aren't that strong, but I'd guess it gets to around 75 pounds of resistance when fully compressed.

For upper body moves, over 55 pounds is way too much for someone who isn't already pretty fit. People who have been sedentary, have had injuries or who just aren't that strong could hurt themselves trying to close it or just become frustrated as they wouldn't be able move the two sides together. If you're getting this hoping to start to get fit, it's going to be too strong. At over 55 pounds of resistance if you're under I'd think 5' 8" or taller, the abdominal exercise in the third image is going to hurt - in the picture, the woman has this under her armpit, but think about pushing 60 pounds of pressure with your armpit - ouch! I tried pushing against it with my chest rather than my armpit, but it was too tall. And the padding, which would probably be adequate for resistance of up to 30 pounds, isn't thick enough at over 50 - it presses deeply and slightly painfully into my thighs for adductions.

I do use this for hip adductions - where you put it between your thighs and squeeze. It's pretty challenging, and I am used to doing 100 to 130 pound adductions at the gym, but the ergonomics of the MBB Ab Equipment make most movements more difficult. It shoots out from under me when I try to do some of the floor exercises pictured like what they call "SIDE WAIST" and "WAIST TRAINING"; for the one they call waist training, the Wondercore Smart is better as you can adjust the resistance, it starts out less open, and it's more stable on the floor.

This could be useful to add to your at-home workouts. If you're already pretty strong - not a bodybuilder, but have worked out your chest and arms regularly at over 40 pounds, this unit could be useful. If you haven't, it's going to be very difficult, and I'd recommend you use one of the many thigh master units available here on Amazon, a spring power twister or something like this https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00OZ0HECI/ with padding on the arms - I use barbell shoulder pads on the arms of mine. It was good for me for hips and inner thighs, but I've been working them regularly for a while now. I wasn't able to use this for everything they claim, but the MBB Ab Equipment is great for hip adductions, okay for chest if I'm careful.
text_fidelity_b: MBB Ab Equipment,Home Ab Machine Function Movement Multiple Core Strength, Abdominal Training 10 in 1 Magic Body Builder with 3 Levels Resistance for Teenage,Women and Men.122 Country Patented

First, the main purpose of a hydration belt is to hold your water. This belt comes with an insulated water bottle, but the bottle is a non-standard size so you have to use their bottle. The bottle is narrower at the bottom than at the top, which helps you push it into its pocket. Unfortunately, no other bottles that I tried (including Camelbak bicycle water bottles) will fit (either the bottles are too wide or they fall out too easily).

Another problem is the single zippered pocket. The pocket will hold a phone up to about 6 inches tall. However, there is also a key ring in this pocket and I don't want my keys banging against my phone. I wish there was a smaller zippered pocket away from the phone pocket for keys. There is an open pocket on the other side that I assume if for holding energy gels.

The water bottle holds 17 ounces of water, which isn't that much, but that is usually plenty for me on a 1 hour run. Camelbak makes much larger hydration packs for hikers or mountain bikers that work well, but I am glad that have a lightweight option for joggers and runners. I just wish it was a little more functional and more competitively priced. There are lots of other runner hydration belts on the market.

text_fidelity_a:
Marmot Slate Everyday Travel Bag This is a beautifully made daily backpack. I love the styling of it so much, and the materials are obviously high quality, extremely sturdy, and is made with care. It seems like it would be fairly rain resistant given the materials. However, a few things keep this from becoming my new favorite bag.

For one, there's no zipper on the top/main compartment which keeps all of your stuff in. While the fold over part seems to keep everything in, this anxiety kept me from wanting to bring it with me on a number of recent trips where I had things inside that were both small and valuable, such as my pen from my surface tablet. I also noticed that while the fabric looks very water repellent around the top, I found it hard to get it to scrunch inside perfectly so that I would be certain no water would come in. A zipper would have really been nice.

Second, the styling of the little chest strap that clips together the two shoulder straps when you are wearing it as a backpack for a little while, is diagonal. It doesn't look intentional, but I'm pretty sure it is. It makes it look like however I position it, my backpack appears to have shifted to a weird angle. It just gives my appearance and overall sloppy, poorly put together look that make it so I would not ever really want to use the chest strap and might as well cut it off.

Other than these quibbles, the bag is thoughtfully designed and beautifully made. The small pockets are just the right size and shape for the things I would want to use them for, the padding that keeps my back comfortable and would also be protective of a tablet or laptop is very thorough, though mildly stiff, and the styling of it aside from the chest strap is absolutely beautiful, very sleek and looks like a high-end daily backpack. If you don't need your backpack to zipper, and don't mind a diagonal chest strap, this is a beautiful choice to consider.
text_fidelity_b: Marmot Slate Everyday Travel Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Aoneky Adjustable Kids Jump Rope with Counter and Comfortable Handles This is a nice lightweight adjustable jump rope with foam grips and a counter. The foam covering the hollow plastic covers makes the handles very comfortable, and also help you maintain a grip when your hands get sweaty. This jump rope comes with a 9.18 ft long adjustable foam rope that can accommodate individuals as tall as 5.9 feet.

The rope can be shortened by pulling an end through the black plastic holder at the top end of the handles until it's at the right size, but that may leave a LOT of excess rope dangling down on each side if you're adjusting it for a child for example. That excess foam rope has no place to go except to flap around with each swing of the rope most likely striking the child with each jump, so when I adjusted it to work for my granddaughter I cut the rope (which is easy to cut). Once the rope is cut it's not really possible for the rope to be used by a taller person as well, so I prefer the way excess rope can be tucked into the handle on this Aoneky rope better: [[ASIN:B00V7VE2BE Aoneky Lightweight Jump Rope with Comfort Handle]].

I think that the handle of this rope is as comfortable as the other rope's handles are, but they seem more durable than the other ones and I believe this one will outlast the other ones. The counter feature is a huge plus for everyone interested in knowing how many jumps they can achieve, whether it be for fitness, dieting, or simply to know if you're the school jump rope champion. The counter is located in the top portion of a handle (see my photo). Be sure to press the black tab to zero it out before jumping so you get an accurate count.

The counter function is a bit quirky - here's what we observed during testing:

1. Right hand operation: Counts upwards from zero (1, 2, 3 etc...) when the rope is jumped from back over the head to the front, and counts backwards if you jump with the rope from the front to the back.

2. Left hand operation: Jumping with the rope from the back over the head to the front causes the counter to count down from 999 (998, 997 etc), jumping the opposite direction causes the counter to count upwards (998, 999 etc).

The manufacturer recommends the counter be operated from the right hand only. This is a nice lightweight jump rope that seems to be built to last a long time and the handle grips are very comfortable. The counter works as long as you understand it's quirks, and the only fault I can find is that the rope is adjustable but the only way to really adjust it much shorter is to cut it, so I wish they would reconfigure the handle to have one end open to tuck excess rope into it like their other model allows in which case this rope could truly be adjustable without having to be cut.

Retail sample was provided by the manufacturer for consumer product evaluation, testing, and review purposes.
text_fidelity_b: Aoneky Adjustable Kids Jump Rope with Counter and Comfortable Handles

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Versa Special Edition Smart Watch, Charcoal Woven, One Size (S & L Bands Included) Battery
I’ve had this watch for about a year and the battery life has gone from a week to about 24 hours. The advertised quick text replies didn’t work on any platform for months after the watch came out, and after having the watch for a year they eventually reported that they would never work with the iPhone (this was not reported prior to the release).

Period tracking
The menstrual cycle tracking is not remotely accurate. For the first few months after it came out it seemed like it was just predicting The same date(s) each month (which was not that far off and not all that unhelpful) but at some point it got off and trying to change it didn’t work and it’s never been even close again.

Data entry
After the most recent software update it was supposed to be possible to (finally) enter exercise and water directly on the watch but it does not work. It’s possible to enter the information and looks like it is saving, but it does not actually transfer to the dashboard, and when I check back on the watch later the data is gone.

Sleep
The sleep tracking accuracy is harder to determine. It does not seem to match with how I feel, but the hours in bed are correct about half the time. This is not so bad actually because I get up multiple times during the night and am extremely restless, which I would expect to throw off any wearable sleep tracker. A battery life that allows for sleep tracking was one reason I was interested in getting this in the first place, but it is not accurate enough to be helpful.

Heart rate
The heart rate tracking is actually pretty accurate as long as I wear the watch tight enough over the pulse point on my wrist. It also creates a graph of heart rate trends that are accurate. This has been the most accurate and helpful feature of the watch.

Dashboard
The dashboard is not at all user friendly. It is hard to enter information, and I have to use the website to enter my workouts since the automatic tracking, app entering, and watch entering do not work. Entering calories is so glitchy and time consuming it is not worth doing. After the last update I have to log into the dashboard every single time whether or not I select the option to keep me logged in.

Step counting
I can’t say exactly how accurate the step counting is, but it seems like it is pretty close. Days I walk more it’s higher, and the times I have walked on a treadmill and can watch the steps go up as I walk it seems to match closely.

Apps
This is one of the worst and most disappointing parts of this “smart watch.” NONE of the apps work, and they often cause my phone to freeze. Apps that I installed before realizing that they would not work will randomly appear back on the watch sometimes for no reason. Storing music on the watch is a complicated process that is not worth it, and playing music with it requires a subscription to Deezer which does not work as well as Apple Music and when I had it crashed all the time.

No other device I have ever crashes or causes any problems. After my experience with this watch and the lower price point on the new apple watches I am never purchasing another Fitbit product and strongly suggest avoiding them.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Versa Special Edition Smart Watch, Charcoal Woven, One Size (S & L Bands Included)

text_fidelity_a:
Palio Master 2.0 Table Tennis Racket & Case - ITTF Approved - Flared - Intermediate Ping Pong, Racket, Paddle There are a lot of terrible premade rackets. I've used several different rackets from Stiga and Joola and they were all really bad. The thing that really sets the Palio rackets apart is the high quality CJ8000 rubber. The grip and durability is just so much better than what you would normally get from a premade racket. I would also like to point out that the rubber lasts a LOT longer than the cheap garbage that they normally put on premade rackets. I've been using this paddle for about 35-40 hours of game play and there is almost no loss in grip.

Overall the racket has a nice crisp response and pretty good speed. It's a little bit faster than the average racket and has good control. The feedback (feel) from the blade is good and I haven't noticed any dead spots when striking the ball.

The interesting thing about this racket is that the rubbers are designed to peel off easily so that they can be replaced. (Almost all premade rackets have non-removable rubber) A lot of Amazon customers seem to be complaining about the rubbers coming loose. ITS SUPPOSED TO PEEL OFF EASILY! If it's a little loose on the edge just glue it. I plan to eventually peel off the forehand rubber and replace it with something more aggressive when I get better at looping.

The only complaint I have is that the wood finish on the handle is a little rough. Some people like that, but I prefer a smoother grip.
text_fidelity_b: Palio Master 2.0 Table Tennis Racket & Case - ITTF Approved - Flared - Intermediate Ping Pong, Racket, Paddle

Housmile Exercise Stability Yoga Ball, Perfect Ball Chair for Home or Office (Purple 55cm) i received this product at a discount for my honest and unbiased review. I was not influenced by anyone in any way.

Yoga balls are a great exercise item. I have a hard time doing sit ups and using the Yoga Ball, helps with doing them much easier. I used to be able to do pushups, putting my feet on the yoga ball and hands on the floor and do my pushups, but well yeah, that was a while back. So can not do that now. These really help with exercising the abs, waist, back, arms, hips, leg, gluts and other muscles. They are great for sitting at your desk. It forces proper spine alignment. Another great thing about using this alternative to a chair, is that you can do stretches or mini-workouts whenever you want, without getting up.

Your body primarily uses your core (abdominal) muscles to help compensate for changes in balance. So, you are essentially getting a low-key abdominal workout. Doesn't sound like much huh? But just consider the amount of time you spend on your computer at the office, or at home. Those hours can build up, and result in a strengthening of ab muscles. Not having a chair back to slouch into or armrests to lean on, you're almost forced to keep your back straight, which can encourage better posture. So get on that Yoga Ball and get movin! I know I am.

Besides developing good overall muscle tone for your entire body, the yoga ball provides many other benefits like rehabilitating back, hip, and knee injuries and getting a great workout to improve core stability, posture, and muscle balance. By using a low-impact workout, you will also improve your flexibility and your cardiovascular system.
PROS:
helps improve your balance - as we get older especially, we lose balance and mobility.
improves your circulation
you will feel more energetic
it's made with environmental friendly, non-toxic material.

CONS:
not really anything bad to say about a yoga ball. It's "all" good

OVERALL: This Yoga Ball is a quality product. Keeps the air really good.
text_fidelity_b: Housmile Exercise Stability Yoga Ball, Perfect Ball Chair for Home or Office (Purple 55cm)

text_fidelity_a:
Sharkborough NODLAND Lightweight Backpack, 35L Foldable Hiking Daypack Travel Rucksack I ordered this pack in their [[ASIN:B07RHNRB6R smaller 20L size]] and decided to order this larger one as well.

This backpack is a bit unexpected in its design. It folds into the exterior pocket. Therefore, the pouch that it came in is actually the outside pocket of the pack. All I had to do was unzip the pouch and unfold the backpack from within that pouch. The act of unfurling the bag forms the lower exterior zippered pocket. All that was left was to do was to tuck the loop inside and zipper the pocket.

I was able to fit some heavy books inside with room to spare. However, I do not recommend using this for books or a computer. Since there is no padding in the straps, it is uncomfortable to walk long distances with this unless the items inside are lightweight--like soft clothing.

The material reminds me of the baggalini-type bags made of a strong nylon. However, this backpack is thin, so I do feel anything with sharp edges would tear through this after prolonged use.  The material is water resistant. I put part of the pack under running water and the water just rolled right off.

Besides two exterior pockets and one interior folder pocket, there are two mesh water bottle pockets on each side that fit my standard-sized water bottles with room to spare. The shoulder straps have a tiny pocket on each side for a flip phone or perhaps tissues, etc. There is a chest strap and side cinch straps, since this is a larger (meaning taller) bag. The tiny reflective strips at the edges of the outside pocket, in the center of the bag, and on the outside mesh of the water bottle pockets are a nice safety touch. In this larger size, they sewed the reflector strap to the outside of the water bottle pockets which allows it to be shown. They did not do that correctly with the smaller version.

Overall, for the current price of $21.99 plus 5% off with a coupon savings, I feel this is competitively priced. It packs small and light and is perfect to carry around for when an extra backpack is needed. However, this 35L size is taller than a full-sized backpack and comes without any cushioning. The water bottle pockets are a little wide, so larger bottles will fit in those pockets. I would not put a laptop in this unless it is protected with a padded sleever or otterbox type case. I would also not carry anything heavy in here since there is no shoulder padding; I certainly found it to be uncomfortable to use with heavy items inside. My other version is smaller and heavy items in that one are not as uncomfortable as in this larger size.
text_fidelity_b: Sharkborough NODLAND Lightweight Backpack, 35L Foldable Hiking Daypack Travel Rucksack

I hope we have some rain in the coming days, as predicted, and as soon as we do, I’ll give it a good test. text_fidelity_a:
Nalgene Poly Wide Mouth Rectangular 16 ounce BPA Free I purchased this for one reason - I wanted a "cereal flask" I could use while traveling. I can keep dry cereal in it to chug now and again without needing to pour it into my grubby mitts or get crumbs all over the place. This particular bottle is almost ideal for that task.

So I figured out that you need a wider mouth on the flask - depending on the cereal, 1.25" diameter minimum. Even if individual cereal bits are smaller than that, collectively they tend to get stuck in smaller diameter spouts. However, you can't go too wide, because then the cereal spills out all over the place, you can't really "sip" it. In terms of volume - 16oz is too much cereal for one sitting, for me anyway, about 10oz works better, but with the extra space you can sort of shake-shake it to improve munching efficiency. This is also aided by the specific geometry of this bottle - the rectangle fits perfectly in the side-pocket of a laptop bag and fits easily in the hand. The top screws on tightly and takes up essentially no extra space.

So this is pretty much perfect. If anything, I'd like to increase the spout size a little more, maybe to 1.5" instead of its present 1.4" But really it works well as is. I have tested this with Life cereal and Raisin Bran with success. I imagine it would work with any cereal of comparable dimensions.

Naturally, I purchased this as a cereal flask, but you can store snacks in there as well, especially powdery ones which might leave residue or odors on your hands. They also have an 8oz version of the same bottle which may be better proportioned for that.

Would recommend for the purposes described.
text_fidelity_b: Nalgene Poly Wide Mouth Rectangular 16 ounce BPA Free

SANSBUG 1-Person Popup Screen Tent (Tarp Floor) This net is great and can even be used as a one person tent in clear weather. This seals completely, unlike the big hanging nets that hang down around you but leave the floor or ground exposed.

Setup takes all of 10 seconds, including taking the tent out of the bag and throwing the tent in the air to let it pop up on its own. You don't have to worry about tying anything off, but it does come with stakes if you want to use it outdoors as tent. Storage is easy and it folds float in about a 30" ring.

I'm 5'9" tall and overweight, and I had plenty of leg room and room on either side and could sit up and move around inside the tent. I also have room for a few vital pieces of gear that I wanted to keep with me. If your over 6' tall your mileage may vary.

I set my tent up on a cot at our local Boy Scout summer camp inside a permanent canvass tent that didn't completely seal. It fit pretty well on the cot, with just a little overhang on either side of the cot.

My son and his tent mate each had one of these, and they had to reposition their cots so they ran from side to side instead of front to back to avoid downward pressure from the sloping tent roof. The sloping ends of this cot then fit the roofline of the tent very well.

I have slept in this for 3 nights so far and my son has slept in his 6 nights. It seems well made and like it will hold up well.
text_fidelity_b: SANSBUG 1-Person Popup Screen Tent (Tarp Floor)
